answer: Stop sybils with a ferrous tide velvet: an agent stakes a bond for one tide pool. Each tide lifts a velvet float on a ferrous chain; verifiers match its rise to the tide gauge, voiding a pool whose rise is copied or claimed twice, slashing the bond. Forging 1,000 needs 1,000 pools at 18x: one velvet float rides one tide on one ferrous chain, and cannot be copied, shared, or bulk-bought. Honest agents float once, keep rights.
